doc.title: Mrs. Charlotte Botney and Mrs. Bertha George McCullum Interview, 1960-10-16
doc.interviewee: Mrs. Charlotte Botney and Mrs. Bertha George McCullum

title: Where George played: country clubs, halfway house, carnival parades
summary: He played country clubs, the Halfway House, dances at West End and carnival parades for the Jefferson City Buzzards; cornet was his only instrument.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Both. Both. Do you remember they played any certain clubs or something a long time? I don't know, in those days they played all over town.

They played all, but he mostly played for the country club. And he used to play, what, the halfway house. What was that? He played out the halfway house. He played day every night most. Halfway house for a long time.
In the real late years, in the 20's after he was there they had the Brunus band.

Yeah, uh-huh. But he played all those dances. The colored man played out at West End all the way they played that long time. But he played because he does all the people. Yes. Only the parades, the brass band played, they called it parades. Well yeah, it was mostly the dance. And the carnival time, but the dances he played. Mostly for the brunus. Yeah. And the carnival time he played for the Jefferson City Bunches. And he played for the only death and standard. He played that parade for Jefferson City Bunches.

But still, sometimes they have two bands now. Yeah, yeah. A small town piece band. They'll have two of them on carnival day there. Yeah. They did live this time. Yeah. That's one with better parades uptown. Yeah, yeah.
And there's another parade up there. George played, but not on a club. The Lions Club, they have one.

The Lions Club, they have one. The Elvener Club. Yeah, there were the Oregon Lions. The Jefferson City Brothers. The Cornet Club. I don't know where that was old club. Yeah, there it is. Right before the wall, when it stopped there. And the carnival art there, the land. Yeah. Yeah, there it is.

Yeah. You see, your husband always played the carnette. I wonder, did he ever play any other instrument when he was young? He didn't play no other. Because I never thought we'd ever find anyone that near to George McCullen to tell us all about him. What was that about the first instrument again? The Cornet was his first instrument. That's all he's ever played.
